points.quote: That’s why every summative assessment in Moodle now includes an AI acknowledgment form. The golden rule is “Own what you submit”.
points.gist: Every summative assessment in Moodle includes an AI acknowledgment form; the golden rule is 'Own what you submit'.

points.quote: You need to acknowledge whenever you use AI to help with an assessment you completed during your own time.
points.gist: You need to acknowledge whenever you use AI to help with an assessment completed in your own time.

points.quote: The form is important. If it is not completed, or not completed accurately, lecturers may need to contact you about your submission.
points.gist: If the form is incomplete or inaccurate, lecturers may need to contact you about your submission.

points.quote: If you skip this dropbox, you can submit the assignment but it won't have an attached declaration, which may be reported.
points.gist: Skipping the dropbox still allows submission, but with no declaration attached, which may be reported.

points.quote: When you submit your assignment in Moodle, you'll choose a checkbox to either state you did or did not use AI in the assessment.
points.gist: On submission in Moodle you choose a checkbox stating whether or not you used AI.

points.quote: Data analysis: using AI to analyse data sets or interpret results
points.anchor: 2. Tell us how you used AI
points.gist: Declaration option: data analysis, using AI to analyse data sets or interpret results.

points.quote: If you select the 'Other' option, you'll explain exactly how you used AI in the 'Other AI usage' text box.
points.anchor: 2. Tell us how you used AI
points.gist: Choosing 'Other' means explaining exactly how you used AI in the text box.

points.quote: You must not AI if you have been told not to do so in the assessment brief. You must not use AI to write or complete your assignments for you.
points.anchor: When is it not appropriate to use AI?
points.gist: You must not use AI if the assessment brief says not to, nor to write or complete your assignments.

points.quote: Claiming AI-generated work to be your own is academic misconduct.
points.anchor: When is it not appropriate to use AI?
points.gist: Claiming AI-generated work as your own is academic misconduct.

points.quote: Your tutors may ask you to discuss your work in person to assess your understanding of what you submitted.
points.anchor: When is it not appropriate to use AI?
points.gist: Tutors may ask you to discuss your work in person to assess your understanding.

points.quote: As a University of Portsmouth student you can access Microsoft Copilot, a generative AI assistant which can help you with a range of tasks from research to planning, and more.
points.gist: Portsmouth students can access Microsoft Copilot, a generative AI assistant.

points.quote: Get feedback on drafts, with your own judgement applied. You may use this feedback to inform and enhance your work.
points.anchor: When is it appropriate to use AI?
points.gist: You may get AI feedback on drafts, applying your own judgement, to inform and enhance your work.

points.quote: The goal isn’t to ban AI or ‘catch you out’, but to make sure your work remains your own.
points.anchor: What does the University expect of you?
points.gist: The goal is not to ban AI or catch students out but to ensure work remains their own.

points.quote: The University offers workshops, examples and short guides to help you learn how to use AI effectively and responsibly.
points.gist: The University offers workshops, examples and short guides on using AI effectively and responsibly.
